title: Quantum Cryptography and Autoformalization in Lean
authors: Maor Ben Shahar, Jonathan Morag, Dirk Englund, Kfir Sulimany
abstract: Quantum key distribution provides secure communication by relying on physics principles and mathematical reasoning. Security proofs across the field can contain gaps, often between individually valid theorems integrated under mismatched assumptions. We produce an end-to-end security theorem formalized in the Lean proof assistant, eliminating hidden hypotheses by building only on Lean's standard axioms. Our proof covers composable security of the entanglement-based qubit BB84 protocol against coherent attacks by the postselection technique, accounting for finite block size, and is written in a language that enforces local operations and classical communication to help ensure a faithful representation of the protocol. The proof itself was enabled by LLM-based autoformalization, and with the proof complete, we used the same pipeline as a discovery machine, reducing the finite-size penalty on the key rate. Our work sets a reproducible standard for security arguments in quantum cryptography and shows how formal proof engines can accelerate discovery across quantum information science.
summary: This paper develops a novel, machine-checkable framework in the Lean proof assistant to prove the end-to-end security of QKD protocols like BB84. By formalizing the entire process, including finite-size effects and coherent attacks, it establishes a reproducible standard for security arguments in quantum cryptography. This showcases how AI-assisted formal methods can accelerate fundamental theoretical discoveries in quantum information science.
main_problem: The core problem is establishing rigorous, end-to-end, composable security proofs for Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols, addressing gaps caused by mismatched assumptions in existing literature.
main_result: The authors provide the first end-to-end, machine-verified composable finite-key security proof for the entanglement-based qubit BB84 protocol against coherent attacks.
method: The work formalizes the entire security argument within the Lean proof assistant, utilizing an LLM-based autoformalization pipeline and enforcing protocol constraints via a specialized Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) language.
model_or_system: The focus is on the theoretical security analysis of the entanglement-based qubit BB84 protocol, modeled using quantum channels and structured as a sequence of local operations and classical communication steps.
key_observables: Security bound ($\epsilon_{	ext{QKD}}$), key rate (addressing finite-size penalty), and the probability of protocol abortion ($	ext{p}_{	ext{abort}}$).
important_parameters: Finite block size, QBER ($q$), and the parameters governing error-correction schemes (e.g., decoding radius $t$).
main_assumptions: The security proof relies on the LOCC framework, the assumption of coherent attacks, and the successful application of finite-size entropy bounds.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the AI-assisted proving workflow (AI agents $	o$ Lean kernel $	o$ manual review). Figure 2 details the machine-checked BB84 development flow from LOCC construction to security proofs.
paper_structure: The paper builds a formal framework in Lean to model quantum protocols as structured types, derives the associated quantum channel using the diamond norm, and applies this framework to prove the security of BB84 by comparing the real channel to an ideal, secure channel.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates a powerful synergy between theoretical quantum information science and formal verification tools, setting a new standard for provable security in quantum communication protocols.
